Meta ads strategy and creative diversification via Andromeda update and campaign consolidation

  

## **Meta Ads Strategy and Andromeda Update**

  - Meta's Andromeda ad retrieval system matches users to personalized ads based on historical data.
  - Broad targeting should be maintained for cold campaigns, leveraging Advantage+ audience optimization to maximize reach.
  - Meta evaluates conversions using multi-click attribution sequences rather than single last-click attribution models.
  - Underperforming ads should remain active if the ad set meets overall performance KPIs.
  - Ad creatives must be evaluated at the ad set level to account for multi-touch attribution.
  - Creative refresh cycles should be triggered when frequency increases and click-through rates decline.

  

## **Creative Volume and Content Diversification**

  - High creative volume and diversification across carousels, looping videos, and static images drive ad performance.
  - Automated content production enables rapid generation of varied visual styles like twilight and moody aesthetics.
  - Advantage+ creative text generations and automated enhancements should be disabled.
  - Placement settings should be manually configured to exclude underperforming placements like the audience network.

  

## **Client Tier Categorization**

  - Tier 2 clients are designated as legacy accounts requiring minimal maintenance and fixed budgets.
  - All future accounts and ICP-aligned clients will utilize advanced multi-creative Andromeda ad strategies.

  

## **Performance Review Cadence and Monitoring Tools**

  - The team will implement a monthly review cadence for creative assets and budget allocations.
  - An AI-driven weekly flag tool will monitor KPIs to identify performance anomalies requiring intervention.
  - Hidden Gem AI will diagnose performance fluctuations and recommend budget adjustments or creative refreshes.

  

## **Website IT migration and DNS management**

  - The client is transitioning from GoDaddy to a private IT company following a security breach.
  - Chiara noted that migrating to the private IT company requires sharing GHL DNS records and subdomains.

  

## **Marketing material design and image usage**

  - The team is developing new marketing materials and website designs for an upcoming event.
  - The client is permitted to use the optimized marketing images anywhere on the website.

### **Summary**

Meta ads strategy and creative diversification via Andromeda update and campaign consolidation  
  
**Meta Ads And Andromeda**  
Andromeda retrieval system prioritizes creative diversification and massive ad volume over traditional interest targeting. Evaluating performance at adset level prevents premature removal of sequencing assets.  
  
**Campaign Structure And Settings**  
Consolidating campaigns into 1 adset optimizes signal distribution for lower budgets. Keeping Advantage+ audience enabled while disabling unwanted text generation maintains control.  
  
**IT Transition And Security**  
Moving from GoDaddy to a private IT company is approved provided specialists receive existing DNS records to avoid conflicts. Incorporating optimized images into website designs proceeds using shared links.

  
  

### **Decisions**

## **Aligned**

  - **Consolidating ad accounts into single ad sets** The team aligned on structuring ad campaigns with a single campaign, a single ad set, and a large volume of ads to consolidate event signals.
  - **Disabling advantage plus placements on ads** The team decided to disable advantage plus placements so they do not test unwanted placements like the audience network.
  - **Disabling advantage plus creative text generation** The team aligned on turning off advantage plus creative text generation because the automated text modifications make minimal performance differences.
  - **Treating legacy tier two clients differently** The team aligned on treating tier two legacy clients differently by maintaining simpler, set-and-forget ad strategies with minimal maintenance.

  
  

### **Next steps**

### **Details**

  - **Meta Ads Strategy and the Andromeda Update Background**: Gillian Conley shared insights on running meta ads and leveraging an artificial intelligence tool, highlighting the Andromeda update as one of the most significant advancements in meta ads over the past five to ten years. Gillian Conley noted that Meta repurposed compute originally purchased for their metaverse virtual world to train new ad models that improve personalized ad delivery ([00:01:27](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.gyodqbixi1am)).
  - **Expert Insights and Ad Volume Benchmarks from Ben Heath and Alex Hormozi**: Gillian Conley discussed insights from YouTube educator Ben Heath, who paid Alex Hormozi $230,000 for advertising insights. Gillian Conley pointed out that while Daniel scales businesses with 160 ads, Alex Hormozi runs 900 ads for their own offer and consults hundreds of businesses through acquisition.com ([00:04:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.zf5r43ollpvn)).
  - **Andromeda Retrieval System and Creative Diversification Requirements**: Gillian Conley explained that Andromeda is an ad retrieval system that customizes personalized ad delivery rather than putting users into broad interest buckets ([00:06:04](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.y34qf93l8v1x)). Chiara Henry and Ananya Arora discussed how advertisers produce massive creative volume (50-plus ads) to achieve better results across different formats like video, statics, carousels, and influencer styles ([00:06:55](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.jmi5zy73pk43)). Gillian Conley concluded that failing to use creative diversification limits market reach to only a small fraction of potential target audiences ([00:07:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.294jrxd9xkhh)).
  - **Artificial Intelligence Training Shifts and the Limitations of Interest Targeting**: Gillian Conley and Chiara Henry discussed how Meta repurposed training ships to build a better ad serving platform that prioritizes transcripts, copy, and historical conversion data over interest targeting ([00:11:14](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.iha7rx1req7c)). Gillian Conley noted that interest targeting has significant downsides because it arbitrarily labels and serves ads, making business similarity scores a more relevant metric ([00:12:17](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.4lnm03kz6cci)).
  - **Creative Sequencing and Frequency Thresholds for Cold Campaigns**: Gillian Conley and Chiara Henry examined creative sequencing and the probability of purchase based on ad viewing frequency ([00:13:20](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.l8qpsk7p4hqy)). Gillian Conley and Chiara Henry noted that showing an identical ad three or four times causes purchase probability to decline massively, whereas introducing novel creatives maintains high purchase probability ([00:14:33](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.w2iqs1g68dlr)). Gillian Conley instructed that checking cold ad frequency levels reveals whether an account suffers from creative fatigue ([00:15:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.4u60bt1pvkka)).
  - **Multi-Click Attribution and Adset-Level Performance Analysis**: Gillian Conley and Chiara Henry addressed the discrepancy between last-click attribution and multi-click review systems, noting that Meta optimizes across ad sequences rather than isolated last clicks. Gillian Conley cautioned against turning off top-of-funnel or middle-of-funnel creatives that appear to have low return on ad spend, because Meta uses them to sequence and drive final purchases ([00:16:40](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.l7e7exoqx1ig)). Gillian Conley emphasized evaluating returns at the adset level rather than individual ad levels ([00:18:43](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.7533dam9v3sc)).
  - **Frequency Benchmarks and Creative Refresh Strategies**: Gillian Conley evaluated frequency benchmarks, noting that a frequency of two or less is critical for cold campaigns targeting new audiences, while warm retargeting campaigns tolerate higher frequencies. Gillian Conley admitted they previously paid little attention to frequency, whereas Shawal Nazir monitored it closely, and established that frequency will guide creative refresh rates and volume ([00:21:48](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.bftt2fy5455t)).
  - **Balancing Creative Volume, Quality, and Budget Constraints**: Ananya Arora questioned how budget impacts creative volume, and Gillian Conley responded that the governing threshold is maximizing creative volume while maintaining a high level of quality ([00:23:30](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.ekoo1p1tbk2r)). Gillian Conley noted that while e-commerce brands with large budgets easily dump 50 to 100 ads, determining the exact ad-to-budget ratio remains challenging, leading them to err on the side of higher creative volume ([00:24:45](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.9dxmawe8q2mj)).
  - **Broad Targeting Strategy and Advantage+ Audience Settings**: Ananya Arora inquired whether broad targeting without specific interests would be applied moving forward, and Gillian Conley confirmed that top-of-funnel campaigns run entirely broad to achieve the highest results ([00:27:41](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.itredkww7bxd)). Gillian Conley explained that old selectable interest groups have been sunsetted by Meta, though lookalike audiences remain useful for specific pools like ideal resort owners ([00:28:58](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.wj3gezi3o7ua)). Gillian Conley noted that Advantage+ audience settings are enabled by default to give Meta flexibility in finding converting users ([00:30:53](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.w1nwwkkjdsxp)).
  - **Sourcing Ad Creatives from Organic Content and Testing Formats**: Gillian Conley discussed sourcing ad creatives from organic content and testing diverse formats such as carousels, looping videos, static videos, and voiceovers rather than relying on slight variations of the same video. Gillian Conley noted that while Alex Hormozi reuses organic podcast clips as ads, their own strategy requires testing multiple distinct ad angles and formats to appeal to different audience segments ([00:33:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.cz952isvyd0u)).
  - **Indicators for Refreshing Creatives and Monitoring Adset Performance**: Chiara Henry asked when to proactively add more creatives, and Gillian Conley answered that declining click-through rates, dropping hook rates, and increasing frequency serve as primary indicators to refresh ads ([00:38:20](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.f0vx08h8vla2)). Gillian Conley added that if a testimonial video consistently receives spend despite low return on ad spend, Meta considers it important for sequencing, whereas ads receiving zero spend should be removed ([00:40:25](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.d16106wtxfrx)).
  - **Campaign Structure and Consolidation for Lower Budgets**: Ananya Arora asked whether to create independent sets or combine creatives, and Gillian Conley stated that due to relatively low budgets, the campaign structure will consist of a single campaign with one adset containing multiple ads to consolidate event signals rather than scattering them across multiple adsets ([00:41:21](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.8ez7zecbtm8g)).
  - **Configuring Advantage+ Settings and Disabling Unwanted Creative Features**: Ananya Arora and Chiara Henry questioned which Advantage+ settings to turn off, and Gillian Conley recommended keeping Advantage+ audience enabled while turning off placements for unwanted networks like the audience network ([00:43:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.pfkapdx5qci0)). Gillian Conley advised turning off Advantage+ creative text generation because text modifications make marginal performance differences and require unnecessary quality checks, while also addressing issues with random related media being added by Meta ([00:45:44](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.7ezjsgnnvnvd)).

  - **Adapting Proprietary Content Styles via Automation and Creative Variations**: Chiara Henry and Gillian Conley discussed whether to use real client footage versus proprietary polished content ([00:48:51](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.hmd5qai8gt80)). Gillian Conley decided that while real footage can be tested, they prefer their proprietary style and will use automation tools to generate diverse stylistic variations—such as golden hour, twilight, moody, and undersaturated tones—across multiple folders to match what performs best ([00:50:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.6i7xx3l1r4oa)).

  - **Client Tiers and Legacy Account Management**: Gillian Conley clarified account management distinctions, instructing that tier two clients are legacy accounts where strategies remain low-touch and set-and-forget, whereas tier one clients and new clients fitting the ideal customer profile receive advanced creative strategies and optimization ([00:54:51](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.oiqvy2i563g8)).
  - **Review Process Cadence and Hidden Gem Artificial Intelligence Flagging Tool**: Gillian Conley outlined the upcoming review process, which will involve a monthly cadence for creative and budget reviews alongside a weekly automated flagging tool created by Shawal Nazir ([00:56:48](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.gkignp81yws1)). Gillian Conley explained that the tool will use Hidden Gem artificial intelligence to analyze key performance indicators, allowing them to quickly adjust budgets or refresh creatives when metrics fall outside expected ranges ([00:57:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.bpe9utf7jmyw)).
  - **Evaluation of AI Note-Taking Application and Data Privacy**: Chiara Henry raised concerns regarding data privacy and ad targeting when connecting personal accounts, such as Gmail and bank accounts, to a new AI note-taking app. Despite expressing hesitation about data sharing for advertising purposes, Chiara Henry noted the app's utility, highlighting features such as character customization, automated emoji messaging, calendar integration, and a security function that flags potential phishing emails ([00:58:50](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.wgm4smgjmpkv)). Furthermore, Jack expressed a willingness to pay for the application ([01:01:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.xwee41jb5p96)). The participants acknowledged the app's security benefits while navigating its data tracking implications ([01:00:11](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.598o0akw6dbw)).
  - **Transition from GoDaddy to Private IT and GoHighLevel Integration**: The team discussed a security breach involving a hacker installing an uploader and malware, prompting Lark to switch from GoDaddy to a private IT company ([01:02:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.1s1bestvm6sf)) ([01:08:41](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.ky5xqc3b2u2b)). Chiara Henry raised a concern about whether this transition would disrupt GoHighLevel DNS records and configurations. To address this, the team determined that the private IT specialist must be informed of existing configurations to avoid conflicts on the shared domain ([01:02:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.1s1bestvm6sf)) ([01:07:06](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.6tawzet7n2ho)). Chiara Henry planned to consult Alicia and review GoHighLevel settings—specifically under sites and subdomains for email and photos—to gather the necessary configuration details ([01:04:15](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.6mg7b8e3n8p8)). Ultimately, moving from GoDaddy to the private IT company was deemed acceptable, provided that the team furnishes the IT specialist with a screenshot of the DNS records and subdomains used through GoHighLevel ([01:08:41](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.ky5xqc3b2u2b)).
  - **Marketing Materials and Website Design for Salesforce Event**: The team discussed the creation of new marketing materials and website design for an event at Salesforce. A key part of this effort involved utilizing specific images previously created by Lark. The participants discussed whether these assets were available for use, and Lark confirmed that their created images could be utilized anywhere on the website. The consensus reached was to proceed with incorporating Lark's optimized images into the new website design and marketing collateral by sharing the appropriate links ([01:04:15](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.6mg7b8e3n8p8)) ([01:08:41](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpv2D1nk5cDoHxTAn7yP0Ff7wheeZJ457OHZVLlrNNI/edit?ouid=106475412914217436338#heading=h.ky5xqc3b2u2b)).
